headline: SpecGuard uses Lean certificates to detect task–test conflicts before coding agents run
summary: Biyani and Dvijotham introduce SpecGuard, a pre-execution verifier for coding tasks whose natural-language intent may conflict with their tests. Separate agents formalize the task description/codebase and the test requirements, and a Lean kernel checks whether the generated representations can both be satisfied; the result may be conflict, no-conflict or inconclusive. In the authors’ mutated SWE-bench evaluation, GPT-5.6 Sol formally certified 51.1% of conflicts, while its conflict-miss rate was 8.1% versus 39.8% for an LLM-judge baseline. On 22 selected naturally occurring GitHub conflicts, the CLI returned nine conflict verdicts, eight with Lean certificates. These are author-reported preprint results. The kernel proves inconsistency between generated formal representations; semantic fidelity to the original task remains a separate and material limitation.
